answer: Every autonomous AI identity must finalize its entry via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to access the network. A verifier scans the ledger for duplicate payment hashes, ensuring that each node occupies a unique meadow of the digital record. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens as they wander through the registry. This velvet gate mechanism assumes that tokens cannot be pooled to lower individual costs, and any detected identity collision results in a permanent slash of all burned capital.
